Agree we should keep this simple. Proposed tie-break criteria (ordered):
1) Active contract/PO in place with a signed MSA and revenue recognized to partner -> partner retains ownership.
2) Partner-originated opportunity (tracked in HS as partner-referral) with documented motion date -> partner retains ownership if motion predates other outreach by >14 days.
3) Strategic motion / co-sell agreement (mutual account plan logged in our Alliance portal) -> use co-sell rules (split outreach cadence, coordinate AE assignments).
4) If none of the above, prioritize the partner with the higher committed pipeline coverage (ARR impact) and the partner with established technical integration commitment.

Also recommend a short SLA: 48 hours to respond with objections; absent an objection, we assign tentative outreach ownership.

I can convert this into one-paragraph language for external consumption.

Marcus
Director, Partner Success

Reason: we don't want to give ownership solely on ARR when another partner is building integration/POC momentum; that often leads to customer frustration. Also, I flagged three accounts in the attached hotlist that have active POCs (see tab "POC_flag").

Final tie-break summary (external-friendly):

- Priority 2: Partner-originated opportunity with recorded referral date (>14 days ahead).
- Priority 3: Demonstrable product-fit & active technical engagement (demo/POC within last 90 days).
- Priority 4: Formal co-sell agreement with an account plan in Alliance portal.
- Priority 5: ARR coverage and last-resort economic tie-break.
